translations.text: Now, renowned man, search earnestly into spiritual mysteries with the power of your mind and the wisdom of your heart, so that you may truly know how it came about, when the Almighty was born through a pure virgin,

after he had chosen Mary, the finest of maidens, the glorious young woman, as his protection, that angels clothed in white garments did not appear there when the Prince came, the hero, into Bethlehem.
Messengers were ready, who then told the shepherds in spoken words and announced true joy: that the Son of the Lord had been born into the world, in Bethlehem.

Yet it does not say in the books that they appeared there in white garments at that noble time, as they did afterwards, when the glorious Lord, the majestic Prince, called his band of thegns, the beloved company, to Bethany.

On that day of joy they did not scorn the word of their teacher, their giver of treasure. At once they were ready, the men with their lord, for the holy city, where the giver of glory revealed many signs to them,
the protector of glory, in mysterious words, before the only-begotten Son, the co-eternal Child, ascended to his own Father, forty days by count after he had risen from death out of the earth.

Through his sufferings he had then fulfilled the words of the prophets throughout the world, as they had sung beforehand. The thegns praised and loved with joy the Lord of life, the Father of all creation.
Afterwards he gave his dear companions a fair reward for this, and the Ruler of angels, the mighty Lord, eager to go to his Father's kingdom, spoke these words: "Rejoice in your hearts!
I will never turn away from you. I will always keep my love for you, and give you power, and stay with you for ever and ever, so that through my grace you will never lack anything good.
Go now through all the vast earth, along the wide ways. Make it known to the multitudes, preach and proclaim the bright faith, and baptize the peoples under the heavens.
Turn to the heathens, destroy their idol-shrines, cast them down and hate them, put out enmity, and sow peace in the minds of men through the abundance of your powers.
I will stay with you from now on as your comfort, and I will keep you in peace with steadfast strength in every place."
Then suddenly a sound was heard, loud in the air. A host of heaven's angels, a beautiful troop, messengers of glory, came in a throng.
Our King went up through the roof of the temple while they watched, the chosen thegns who were still following in the footsteps of the beloved one at that meeting-place.

They saw their Lord, the Son of God, rise up from the earth on high. Their spirits were sad, burning in their hearts, their minds mourning, because they could no longer see one so dear to them under the sky.
Heavenly messengers raised a song. They praised the Prince, lauded the Author of life, and rejoiced in the light that shone from the Saviour's head.
They saw two all-bright angels shining beautifully in their adornments around the First-born, the glory of kings.
With wondrous words and a bright voice the angels called down from on high over the crowd of men: "Why are you waiting, men of Galilee, standing in a circle?

"Now you clearly see the true Lord go into the sky. The possessor of victory, the foremost of princes, the creator of all peoples, will ascend from here to his homeland with this band of angels, to the Father's native throne."

With this company we will bring the Lord over the vaults of the heavens to the bright city, with this joyful band. He is the best and noblest of all the children of victory, the one you are gazing at here and see with joy, shining in his adornments.
Yet he will come again himself to seek out the nations of the earth with a vast host, and then he will judge every deed that the peoples under the heavens have done."

Then the Guardian of glory, the King of archangels, the protector of the saints, was surrounded by clouds, up above the roofs. Hope was renewed, and joy in the cities, through the coming of that hero.
Triumphant, the eternal Author of blessedness sat down at the right hand of his own Father.
Then the brave-hearted men went to Jerusalem, into the holy city, sad at heart, from the place where they had last seen God, their giver of joy, rising up before their eyes.
Then the greatest of feasts took place in glory. It was very fitting that thegns, brightly clothed, a beautiful troop, came to that joy in the prince's city.
Now the Saviour of souls, God's own Son, will seek the gift-throne of spirits, after the battle-play.
Peace shall be shared between angels and men from now on, forever and for all time. There is a covenant between God and men together: holy faith, love, the hope of life, and the joy of all light."
For all this we must give thanks and praise to our Lord, and above all for the salvation that he gave us as our hope,
One can make a steeled sword, a weapon. One knows the course of the plains, the far-reaching roads. So the Ruler, God's Son on earth, deals out his gifts to us.
Of this the prophet said that holy jewels were raised up high, bright stars of heaven, the sun and the moon. What are those jewels, so shining, but God himself?
The moon shines over the world, a spiritual star; so God's church shines brightly through the gathering together of truth and righteousness.
As it says in books, after God's Son, King of everything pure, ascended from the earth, the church here endured persecution by lawbreakers under the power of heathen shepherds.
There the sinful enemies paid no heed to truth or to the spirit's need, but they broke and burned God's temple, shed blood, hated and struck down.
Yet through the gift of the Spirit the glory of God's thegns came forth after the ascension of the eternal Lord.
The first leap was when he came down into a woman, a spotless maiden, and there took on human form without sin, which became a comfort to all who dwell on earth.
The third leap, the rush of the King of heaven, was when he climbed onto the cross, Father, Spirit of comfort. The fourth leap was into the tomb, when he gave up the tree, fast in the earthen house.
Therefore we must always scorn idle desires and sin-wounds, and rejoice in what is better.
No one of the race of men on earth need fear the devils' arrows, the spear-attack of the fierce ones, if God, Lord of hosts, shields him.

Then C [rune ᚳ: cen 'torch', or perhaps 'the bold one'? [?]] will tremble; he will hear the King speak, the Ruler of the heavens, speak harsh words to those who formerly obeyed him poorly in the world, while Y [rune ᚣ: yr? [?]] and N [rune ᚾ: nyd 'need'? [?]] could most easily find comfort.
There many a one, frightened and weary, must wait in that place for what fierce punishments he will decree for him according to his deeds.
W [rune ᚹ: wyn 'joy'] of the earth's adornments will be gone. U [rune ᚢ: ur 'our'?] share of life's joys, F [rune ᚠ: feoh 'wealth'] on earth, was long enclosed by L [rune ᛚ: lagu 'water'] by floods.
Then the adornments must burn in the fire; the bright, swift red flame will rage, will stride fiercely across the wide world. The plains will fall, the cities will burst apart.
The fire will be on the move; the greediest of spirits will burn up without pity the ancient treasures that men once held, while they had pride on earth.
It will be a serious matter when he comes again, fierce and righteous. The sky will be shaken, and the great expanses of the world will tremble then.
The terror of the people will be heard loudly with the noise of heaven, the cry of the mourners; those who trust weakly in their works will weep with anxiety before the face of the eternal Judge.
where he may hide himself in that victorious host, when the Lord of hosts, the chief of princes, judges all, the loved and the hated, giving reward according to right to every nation.
We have great need to think earnestly about the beauty of the soul in this barren time, before that terror and dread.
Now it is most like this: as if we were sailing in ships on the flood, over cold water, across the wide sea, travelling on sea-horses, on flood-wood.

That stream on which we toss here is perilous, waves beyond measure, windy seas over the deep way, throughout this feeble world. Our life was hard before we had sailed to land over the rough ridge of the sea.

Then help came to us, which led us to the harbour of salvation: God's spiritual Son. He gave us grace so that we may know, over the ship's side, where we must tie up our sea-horses, our old wave-steeds, made fast with anchors.
